text:
ashwin: heads-up — seeing inconsistent KMS audit coverage for Vault unwraps across regions since ~14:05 UTC. Some unwraps show in KMS logs, others missing. might be RBAC/forwarder gap.

maria: hmm, saw a small spike in credential-access alerts earlier, could be related. do you have sample event ids?

ashwin: here are two samples from vault logs (redacted):
```
vault: 2026-03-22T14:04:59Z unwrap event: key=projects/ai-prod/locations/us-east1/keyRings/rdrw/cryptoKeys/wrap-key v=3 ctx="vault/transit/unwrap"
vault: 2026-03-22T14:05:01Z unwrap event: key=projects/ai-prod/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/rdrw/cryptoKeys/wrap-key v=3 ctx="vault/transit/unwrap"
```
first one shows a matching KMS audit entry, second one has no KMS log in our audit export.

sec-oncall: can you paste the KMS audit search you ran? I can query stackdriver/bigquery for missing events.

ashwin: I did a quick gcloud audit query:
```
resource.type="kms_crypto_key" AND protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricDecrypt" AND timestamp>"2026-03-22T14:00:00Z"
```
it returned only the us-east1 hits. europe-west1 unwraps are absent.

maria: our audit-forwarder logs show a transient error around 14:03-14:07, backlog processing restarted. excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-22T14:03:10Z] audit-forwarder ERROR: grpc stream closed: rpc error: code = INTERNAL desc = connection reset by peer
[2026-03-22T14:04:30Z] audit-forwarder INFO: reconnecting, resuming from offset 1287412
[2026-03-22T14:06:15Z] audit-forwarder WARN: missing record for europe-west1 partition 7, skipping gap > 5s
```
looks like the forwarder skipped a window for that region.

tanvi: okay—so this is likely a pipeline forwarding gap, not immediate RBAC compromise. still need to triage blast radius: which services used europe-west1 key? list below from KMS policy.

maria: services using europe-west1 wrap-key: vault-transit (primary for eu customers), partner-ingest, metrics-archiver. I suggest we: 1) snapshot current audit export, 2) attempt replay from forwarding service offsets, 3) if replay fails, run targeted rewrap for ciphertexts created in the gap window, and 4) rotate ephemeral key version as safety.

sec-oncall: agreed. immediate steps I can run now: pull forwarder consumer offsets, try a manual replay. running: `kubectl exec -n infra audit-forwarder-0 -- ./bin/forwarder admin offsets --namespace eu-west1`

sre-bot: deploy event: audit-forwarder v2.8.1 rolled to 3 replicas at 2026-03-22T14:07:40Z :rocket:

auditor-bot: automation note: created backup snapshot gs://redwood-audit-backups/2026-03-22/3945670000-snapshot.json (size=12MB)

ashwin: replay attempt result: forwarder was able to rehydrate ~90% of missing events, but 12 entries for europe-west1 partition 7 had processing errors: `decode failed: unknown proto field` — likely transient proto mismatch from a partner-produced event.

maria: for the 12 errored unwraps we should do targeted verification: 1) identify corresponding Vault ciphertext IDs, 2) mark related secrets for rewrap/rotation, 3) notify owners. Tanvi, can you help map event->secret?

tanvi: on it. pulling vault audit for that 14:04-14:06 window and matching unwrap IDs now.

sec-oncall: to reduce risk today we should: a) schedule immediate 1-hour write freeze for vault-transit in eu region, b) create a new key version (v4) for wrap-key and update aliases, c) rewrap all ciphertexts with creation timestamp in gap window to v4, d) rotate any ephemeral tokens issued during that window. agreed?

maria: yes, but prefer staged approach: start with readonly freeze and rewrap only for secrets with high-sensitivity tags. full write freeze if mapping shows partners affected.

ashwin: I can run the rewrap job once we have a list. sample commands I will use: 
```
# create new key version
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=wrap-key --keyring=rdrw --location=europe-west1 --project=ai-prod
# rewrap (pseudocode)
for id in list_of_ciphertexts:
  vault write -field=ciphertext transit/rewrap ciphertext=$id new_key=projects/ai-prod/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/rdrw/cryptoKeys/wrap-key/cryptoKeyVersions/4
```
ensure we keep atomic mapping so apps can still unwrap with old v3 during in-flight window.

auditor-bot: checklist: created ticket SEC-5678 for owner notification, added tag `needs-rewrap`, and scheduled 30m follow-up at 2026-03-22T15:00:00Z.

tanvi: mapped 9 of the 12 unwraps to secrets with low sensitivity (metrics), 3 mapped to partner-ingest API creds (high sensitivity). I'll DM owners and escalate for immediate rotation.

sec-oncall: good. action list recap:
- tanvi: inform owners + rotate partner creds now.
- ashwin: prepare rewrap job and smoke-test unwrapping against v4 (do not run global rewrap yet).
- maria: attempt binary replay for the 3 remaining events and capture raw payloads.
- sec-oncall: authorize read-only freeze if more than 5 high-sensitivity secrets are affected.

ashwin: on it. will post back with rewrap dry-run output in ~20m.

maria: FYI raising a small follow-up item for infra: add stricter proto validation and a replay retry queue in audit-forwarder to avoid skipping gaps. filing INFRA-3321.

sec-oncall: thanks team. @sre-bot please keep an eye on forwarder cpu/memory and alert if OOM spike recurs.

sre-bot: monitor configured: watch audit-forwarder memory RSS > 400Mi triggers alert to #eng-sre.

ashwin: dry-run succeeded for a sample secret (unwrap + rewrap -> unwrap ok). rewrap plan ready. executing on high-sensitivity list now, will report success/fail per secret.

(END)
